Transform matching parts

Source: R/transform_matching.R
transform_matching.Rd

These animations map the parts of mobject and target_mobject to keys and transform parts with equal keys into each other. TransformMatchingShapes() matches submobjects by shape (their points after moving to the origin, scaling to height 1 and rounding to three decimals); TransformMatchingTex() matches the parts of MathTex() objects by their TeX strings.

Usage

TransformMatchingShapes(mobject, target_mobject, ..., use_override = TRUE)

TransformMatchingTex(mobject, target_mobject, ..., use_override = TRUE)

Arguments

mobject

The starting mobject.

target_mobject

The target mobject.

...

Named arguments: transform_mismatches, to transform unmatched parts into each other with Transform(); fade_transform_mismatches, to transform them with FadeTransformPieces(); key_map, an optional named character vector or list mapping keys of source parts to keys of target parts that should be transformed into each other although they differ (useful with TransformMatchingTex()); and arguments passed to the part animations, for example path_arc or run_time.

use_override

FALSE ignores an animation override set with override_animation() on the class of mobject.

Details

Unless transform_mismatches or fade_transform_mismatches is TRUE, unmatched parts of the source fade out toward the unmatched target parts, and unmatched target parts fade in from there.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
Anagram <- manim_scene(function(self) {
  src <- Text("the morse code")
  tar <- Text("here come dots")
  self$play(Write(src))
  self$wait(0.5)
  self$play(TransformMatchingShapes(src, tar, path_arc = PI / 2))
  self$wait(0.5)
})
} # }
